aiSummary.headline: Control vs. transition: PSG's territorial dominance meets Marseille's league-high counter threat.
aiSummary.summary: Across the demo dataset, PSG have generated the most xG in Ligue 1 (15.9 in 7) and concede few clear chances at home (3 goals in 4). Marseille are the league's most direct side — 3.1 counter-attack shots per game — and have scored in every match this season. The most informative signals point to PSG controlling territory, but Marseille's set-piece output (5 goals) and transition speed make this less one-sided than the table suggests. Rivalry fixtures have historically produced higher card counts and late goals, which widens the range of plausible outcomes.

signals.label: Home control
signals.detail: PSG unbeaten at home in Ligue 1 (W3 D1); 66% average home possession.

signals.label: Chance quality
signals.detail: PSG xG differential +9.1 vs Marseille +3.7 across 7 matches.

signals.label: Transition threat
signals.detail: OM lead the league in counter-attack shots; PSG's high line has conceded 4 of 6 goals in transition.

signals.label: Set pieces
signals.detail: Marseille have 5 set-piece goals — joint-most in the division.

signals.label: Fixture congestion
signals.detail: PSG played a Champions League away game 4 days ago; Marseille had a full week.

signals.label: Rivalry volatility
signals.detail: Last 6 meetings averaged 5.2 cards and 2 of them were decided after the 75th minute.

expert.title: Why the first 20 minutes decide Le Classique
expert.excerpt: Marseille's best path is to survive PSG's opening press and attack the space behind a high full-back line. If they can't, the game state turns quickly.
body: Watching PSG's last four home matches, the pattern is clear: they set an extreme territorial tempo early, with the full-backs pushed into midfield and the ball recovered within eight seconds of a loss. Opponents who couldn't play through that first wave were behind by half-time in three of four games.

Marseille are better equipped than most to punish it. Their wide forwards stay high and narrow, and they've been the league's most dangerous side on the break. The key duel is OM's left winger against PSG's right-back, who has been caught upfield more than any other defender in the side.

My read: PSG are the stronger team and should control the ball, but this is a fixture where I'd want to see the line-ups before forming a strong view. A Marseille side that starts with two pacy wide players and a target striker for set pieces is a very different proposition from the possession-heavy XI they used at Lille.

risks.title: Line-up uncertainty
risks.detail: PSG's first-choice centre-back is a late fitness test after a minor knock in midweek. Official XIs drop ~60 min before kick-off.

risks.title: Rotation after Europe
risks.detail: PSG played away in the Champions League 4 days ago; partial rotation in midfield is plausible.

risks.title: Rivalry discipline
risks.detail: Red cards in 2 of the last 6 meetings. A dismissal changes every pre-match signal.

risks.title: Small sample size
risks.detail: Seven league matches is early-season data; home/away splits rest on 3–4 games each.

risks.title: Weather
risks.detail: Light rain forecast in Paris — minor effect on passing tempo.
